transcript: Tonight I celebrated my birthday attending Fat Ham with my friends Tony and PJ. I saw it last summer off Broadway at The public and it was one of my favorite things that I saw all year. And the second time around, it continues to be spectacular. It's a loose spin on hamlet, set at a backyard barbecue. And this stories hamlet is a queer college kid named juicy. On a day that's meant to celebrate the union of his mom and his late father's brother, juicy is feeling anything but festive. Fed Him is largely about trying to overcome generational trauma and generationally instilled expectations. There's some really phenomenal writing, which is funny and thought provoking and expertly performed by a cast of mostly Broadway debuts, which is super exciting. There are also a lot of unexpectedly theatrical moments which are incorporated throughout the production really creatively. Overall, the show is just really well written, performed, directed, designed. And it is also 1000 percent of feel good show. I laughed and appreciated and was incomplete all of what I witnessed and experienced. And you will be too when you see it. With that, another playable for my collection.
